body.heading: Make word dice
paragraphs: Your adult helps you fold paper into cubes. On one cube, write who-words: the cat, a giant, my grandma, the robot. On another, write doing-words: dances, snores, juggles, swims.
On a third cube, write where-words: in the bath, on the moon, under the table, at the zoo. Your dice are loaded with silliness.

body.heading: Roll a sentence
paragraphs: Roll all three dice and read your sentence out loud: The robot juggles on the moon. Every roll builds a new sentence.
Some sentences are funny because they could never happen. Some are funny because they nearly could. Both kinds deserve a good laugh.

body.heading: Add more dice
paragraphs: Make a fourth cube with describing words — sleepy, enormous, sparkly, upside-down — and slot them into your sentences.
You are learning how sentences are built, one silly roll at a time. Grammar has never been this giggly.

takeaway: Rolling word dice builds brand-new sentences, and the silliest ones teach you how sentences work.
safetyNotes: An adult should help fold and cut the dice. Sentences must stay kind — no making fun of real people.
screenFreeExtension: Act out your silliest sentence while your family guesses which sentence it was.
